title: Paying a Rural Home Loans Escrow Shortage in One Sum — Member Handover Card
content:
An escrow shortage on a Rural Home Loans loan may be paid by the member at once, by a one-time debit of the member's own account, so that no shortage spread is added to the monthly payment; the shortage is figured on the escrow account as it stands when the member pays.

## When the shortage is fixed

The shortage paid at once is fixed only after no monthly payment on the loan stands unpaid past its due date.

Restated: while any monthly payment on the loan stands unpaid past its due date, the shortage paid at once is not yet fixed.

## What the payment does

The member authorises a one-time debit of their own account for the amount given, which is deposited to the loan's escrow account as a lump-sum shortage payment dated today. The escrow balance rises by that amount, the deposit shows in the escrow activity as a shortage payment, and no shortage spread is added to later monthly payments for it.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `pay_escrow_shortage_8ff65e44`, a tool the customer themselves runs: the agent unlocks it and hands it over to the member, who runs it to authorise the debit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `loan_id` | the loan number of the Country Home loan, as the servicing agent reads it out from the loan record | identifier |
| `shortage_amount` | the shortage being paid, as the agent states it | USD, 2 decimal places, always positive |

## Return

A dictionary receipt: `escrow_txn_id` (reference number of the shortage deposit, a string); `amount` (the deposit, USD to 2 decimal places); `escrow_balance` (the escrow balance after the deposit, USD to 2 decimal places); and `status` ("deposited" when the payment is on the escrow account).

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

On an escrow balance of 320.00, a shortage payment run with `shortage_amount` 1450.00 returns `amount` 1450.00, `escrow_balance` 1770.00 and `status` "deposited".
